The first reaction involves a Michael addition of 2-ethyl-2,6-dimethylcyclohexan-1-one to ethyl acrylate using t-BuOK. The bulky base selectively deprotonates the less hindered α-carbon at C6 (C2 has no α-hydrogens). The resulting enolate attacks ethyl acrylate at the β-position, giving a product where the propanoate chain is attached at C6. Naming the cyclohexyl ring with the attachment point as C1, the carbonyl is at C2, and the substituents are at C1 (methyl) and C3 (ethyl, methyl), yielding ethyl 3-(3-ethyl-1,3-dimethyl-2-oxocyclohexyl)propanoate.

The second reaction is a Michael addition of the nitronate anion from 1-nitropropane (KOH) to (E)-but-2-enenitrile. The nucleophile attacks the β-carbon (the one bearing the methyl group) of the α,β-unsaturated nitrile. After protonation, the product is CH₃CH₂CH(NO₂)CH(CH₃)CH₂CN, which is named 3-methyl-4-nitrohexanenitrile.

Matching these products with the options gives (D).

Answer: D
